top_picks.title: A frontier model edited 0.016% of a small model's weights, with no training, and raised MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1%
top_picks.author: Rikiya Takehi
top_picks.summary: GPT-6 Astra edited 131,072 of Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights (64 MLP output columns in each of layers 15 and 19) with no gradient training. The authors report MATH-500 rising from 7.9% to 48.1%, IFEval from 21.0% to 62.3% and GSM8K from 13.8% to 67.1%, with answers hitting the token limit falling from 93.0% to 33.1%. Hugging Face's ML Intern rebuilt the edit, hash-checked it and measured 51.0% on the full MATH-500 within a day; Simon Willison and Daniel van Strien ran related weight experiments the same week. An X community note adds that the model was handed the weights as text and used code and forward passes, and that the edit mainly fixed repetition loops in thinking mode.
key_takeaways: The edit touched 131,072 weights, 0.016% of the model, in two layers.
Astra used 50 forward passes and practice problems from training sets; evaluation sets were unseen.
Hugging Face reproduced the checkpoint on 2026-11-02 and measured 51.0% on MATH-500.
The largest gain comes from ending reasoning loops: answers hitting the 32,768-token cap fell from 93.0% to 33.1%.
suggested_actions: Open the Hugging Face demo and compare the base and edited Qwen3.5-0.8B on a few of your own prompts.
Point a coding agent at a small local model that loops on your task and ask it to find and ablate the looping direction.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: hand an agent a small model that misbehaves on your own task, give it a budget of forward passes and a few dozen example prompts, and ask it to edit the weights directly. Daniel van Strien did this for an OCR model in under 3 hours for about $10 of compute.
top_picks.why_it_matters: Frontier models are now producing working edits to neural network weights, and the result was copied by independent teams within 24 hours.

top_picks.title: Claude adds Personal Finance: read-only bank connections, two years of transactions, charts and duplicate-charge checks
top_picks.author: Claude
top_picks.summary: Personal Finance in Claude is a US beta for Pro, Max and Ultra subscribers. Accounts connect read-only through Plaid, Claude can see up to two years of transactions, and it categorizes spending, spots duplicate charges and builds charts on request. The launch post drew 11.5M views.
key_takeaways: Available in the US as a beta on Pro, Max and Ultra plans.
Connection is read-only through Plaid, with up to two years of transaction history.
Typical jobs: categorize spending, find duplicate charges, chart trends.
suggested_actions: Connect one account and ask for a recurring-charge audit with a cancel list.
Ask for a chart of spending by category over the past 12 months.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: ask your assistant for a one-page monthly money review (recurring charges, duplicates, three categories that grew) and keep it as a standing prompt. The same pattern works for a small business's card statements.
top_picks.why_it_matters: Mainstream assistants are moving from chat to doing a personal money task end to end, with the user's real data.

secondary_urls.label: Anthropic: Introducing Personal Finance in Claude

top_picks.title: Perplexity Computer ran a $30,000 ad test for Get Maine Lobster: 3.5x the revenue of the non-AI campaign and 63% higher ROAS
top_picks.author: Perplexity
top_picks.summary: Get Maine Lobster put $30,000 into a head-to-head test. The campaign run with Perplexity Computer spent 2.1x as much as the non-AI campaign, brought in 3.5x the revenue and delivered a 63% higher return on ad spend. Computer analyzed creative, produced static ads, made video ads with Higgsfield and posted a daily PDF report to Slack.
key_takeaways: Test budget was $30,000; Computer's campaign spent 2.1x the control and returned 3.5x the revenue.
ROAS was 63% higher than the non-AI campaign.
The loop covered creative analysis, static ads, video ads and a daily Slack report.
suggested_actions: Pick one product and ask an agent to analyze your last 30 days of ad creative, then draft ten statics and three video concepts.
Set up a daily Slack PDF of spend, revenue and top creative.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: split a modest budget between your current campaign and an agent-run one with the same product and audience, and let the agent own creative analysis, new ads and the daily report. Compare ROAS after two weeks.
top_picks.why_it_matters: A small food retailer got a measured, budgeted comparison, with the numbers published on a case-study page.

top_picks.title: Physical Superintelligence reports a proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, accepted by Lean
top_picks.author: Physical Superintelligence
top_picks.summary: Physical Superintelligence says its internal system, running a non-public Anthropic model, had a complete proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture by day 3 of the effort. Lean accepted the proof, and accepted the improved final version as well. The research page links the proofs and code.
key_takeaways: Lean, a proof checker, accepted both the first complete proof and the improved version.
A complete proof existed by day 3 of the run.
Proofs and code are linked from the company's research page.
suggested_actions: Open the research page and read the Lean files.
Run your own open conjecture or lemma through a prover plus a checker loop.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: pair any reasoning model with a formal checker so every claim it makes is machine-verified before you read it. This works for contract logic, spreadsheet models and proofs.
top_picks.why_it_matters: A long-open problem in quantum complexity theory has a machine-checked proof, and the authors publish the files.

top_picks.title: Claude helped solve the first 3D structure of a bacteriophage vault particle: 96 protein copies, about 9.5 MDa
top_picks.author: Anthropic
top_picks.summary: Anthropic's science team used Claude to determine the first 3D structure of a bacteriophage L05 vault, built from 96 copies of one protein and about 9.5 MDa in mass. The shell measures roughly 54 by 45 nm and holds around 25% more volume than the mammalian vault. Structure determination took days rather than the weeks to months it takes manually.
key_takeaways: First 3D structure of a bacteriophage L05 vault.
Structure determination took days instead of weeks to months.
The shell holds roughly 25% more volume than the mammalian vault.
suggested_actions: Read the write-up for the step-by-step division of labor between scientist and Claude.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: break your slowest expert workflow into numbered steps and give the agent the repetitive middle steps while the specialist reviews the outputs.
top_picks.why_it_matters: A months-long structural biology task now fits in a few days with an AI collaborator.

secondary_urls.label: Anthropic: Investigating vault particles with Claude

top_picks.title: ChatGPT Images 2.6 adds GIFs, SVG export and 50% faster generation, with two new API models
top_picks.author: OpenAI
top_picks.summary: ChatGPT Images 2.6 generates GIFs, exports SVG, and runs about 50% faster. The API gets GPT-Image-2.6 Flare, which can return in as little as 6 seconds at low quality, and Sunburst, plus image markup and a complexity parameter. It is available in ChatGPT and Codex on all tiers.
key_takeaways: GIF output and SVG export are new.
Generation is about 50% faster.
API models: GPT-Image-2.6 Flare (as fast as 6 seconds at low quality) and Sunburst.
Available to all ChatGPT and Codex tiers.
suggested_actions: Ask for a looping GIF of your logo and an SVG version of the same mark.
Test Flare on a batch of thumbnails.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: generate an SVG icon set and animated GIF stickers for a product launch in one sitting, and keep the prompts as a reusable brand kit.
top_picks.why_it_matters: Creators and small shops get editable vector output and fast drafts from the same chat window.

top_picks.title: OpenAI shows ChatGPT and Codex drafting CAD, drawings and simulations; two people designed a Codex device in under a week
top_picks.author: OpenAI
top_picks.summary: OpenAI says its models now help engineers create and revise CAD models, prepare manufacturing drawings, set up simulations and finite element analysis, and review designs. As a test, two team members designed a talk-to-Codex hardware device with Astra in under a week, and a contract manufacturer built a small batch of prototypes in under a month. Chip Ganassi Racing is turning 3D scans into editable CAD and drawings, and Mazda is exploring vehicle designs through simulation.
key_takeaways: Astra handled enclosure, PCB, firmware and UI work on the test device.
Prototypes were built in under a month.
Racing and automotive teams are already using it for scan-to-CAD and simulation.
suggested_actions: Describe a gadget you want, ask for an enclosure CAD and a parts list, then 3D print it.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: scan a part you need, ask the agent for an editable CAD file and drawing, and send it to a local print shop. Hardware prototypes now fit a side-project week.
top_picks.why_it_matters: Hardware design is following software toward agent-assisted iteration.

sections.description: Builder wins, success stories and patterns worth copying.

items.title: Infinite Slop TV: 17.8M clip views, 47K people made videos, $8,500 in prizes paid, in under three months
items.author: Pieter Levels
items.summary: Pieter Levels shut down Infinite Slop TV after August to October 2026. His retrospective lists 210,196 clips aired, 17.8M clip views, 47K people who made videos, 185K visitors, 860 hours of video, 3 sponsors and $8,500 in prizes. fal sponsored GPU capacity for the run after speeding up MiniMax's H3.
key_takeaways: Anyone could type into a chat that fed a perpetual live AI video stream.
Faster-than-real-time generation made the format possible.
Sponsors covered GPU capacity and prize money.
suggested_actions: List which part of your product would work as a public live stream that visitors steer.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: put a shared prompt box in front of a live generation pipeline, pay small prizes for the best outputs, and let sponsors fund the compute.

items.title: Instinct, a text-message agent, found an EU rule owed a delayed traveler 600 euros and the claim paid $700
items.author: Deedy
items.summary: Deedy Das texted Instinct about a 6-hour flight delay on a trip from Europe. It cited the EU compensation rule, he exchanged emails for a month, and he was paid out.
key_takeaways: The agent identified the specific entitlement from a plain text message.
Payout took about a month of email exchanges.
suggested_actions: Text your assistant the next time a flight, delivery or bill goes wrong and ask what you are owed.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: keep a standing prompt, 'what am I owed here?', for every delayed trip and bad charge, and collect the payouts.

items.title: A favorite agent prompt: location-based reminders that keep nagging until you confirm
items.author: Thariq
items.summary: Thariq's example asks the agent to track laundry and, if it has been more than 5 days, remind him 30 minutes after he gets home on a weekday until he confirms or delays.
suggested_actions: Write one recurring-chore reminder with a trigger, a delay and a stop condition.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: write chores as trigger, delay and stop rules, and let the agent nag until done.

items.title: ReturnWitness holds a $340 refund until a camera check and a human approve it
items.author: Sidra Miconi
items.summary: A returns-desk tool built on Meta's SAM 3.1 for tracking, custom counting code and Muse models for review. The demo catches a missing lens on a camera kit, holds the refund and lets a person override.
suggested_actions: Pick one counter or bench in your shop where items are checked by eye and film it for a pilot.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: point a camera at the packing bench, let vision count items against the slip and flag mismatches, and keep refund release with a person.

items.title: One Cult.fit engineer rebuilt internal dashboards over a weekend with Codex, saving over $100,000 a year
items.author: Derrick Choi
items.summary: Cult.fit runs 708 centers across 77 cities. OpenAI's case study says non-engineering teams there built more than 20 internal apps with Codex.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: list your five costliest software subscriptions and ask one person to rebuild the most-used dashboard with an agent over a weekend.

items.title: Alex Finn lists the automations he handed to Grok Bot, including watching AI company accounts every 15 minutes
items.author: Alex Finn
items.summary: After a couple of months of daily use he calls it the best AI agent he has used and shares examples to copy, starting with an X plugin watching AI company accounts around the clock.
suggested_actions: Copy the 15-minute monitoring pattern for the five accounts you follow most.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: have an agent watch a short list of accounts every 15 minutes and ping you only when something changes.

items.title: A 50-person company across 12 countries runs product work through agents: voice note, spec, Linear ticket, competitor scan
items.author: Greg Isenberg
items.summary: Greg Isenberg's stack: a voice note to Grok Bot, a grill-me skill that interrogates the idea, a spec sent to Linear through MCP, and research agents reading every competitor's site, pricing and changelog.
suggested_actions: Run the grill-me step on your next feature idea before writing a spec.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: chain voice note, interview-the-founder skill, ticket and competitor scan so an idea turns into a tracked spec in one sitting.

items.title: A daily marketing loop reads analytics, Search Console, Ahrefs and competitors, suggests site changes, and learns from approvals
items.author: Jon Yongfook
items.summary: Jon Yongfook approves or rejects each suggestion, the agent executes the approved ones and adjusts, and it now runs daily across his portfolio of sites.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: build an approve-or-reject queue where the agent proposes site changes and learns from your choices.

items.title: After one week, the $200 plans are enough for great work, and this is the most expensive intelligence will ever be
items.author: Thariq
items.summary: Thariq's takeaway after a week on a $200 plan: you do not need unlimited tokens to do serious work.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: trial a top-tier plan for one month on your highest-value project and measure what you shipped.

items.title: Creator apps such as Instagram Edits and Roblox Studio are shipping with built-in MCPs
items.author: Thariq
items.summary: Agents can do part of the work while power users continue in the tools they already know.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: connect your agent to the editing app you already use through its MCP and hand it the rough-cut work.

items.title: A local Qwen 3.8 27B on a laptop identified Pong and Breakout from raw network weights, with no tools
items.author: Simon Willison
items.summary: Simon Willison fed raw weights of small game-playing networks to Qwen 3.8 27B in LM Studio. It named Breakout with 88% confidence in 52 minutes and Pong with 75% in about an hour, and missed Freeway. Kimi K3.1 Pro got Breakout in 9 minutes 41 seconds.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: ask a local model to describe an artifact it was never trained to read, and see how far it gets before spending on a bigger one.

items.title: Claude Opus edited 0.0085% of an OCR model's weights to stop repetition loops, in under 3 hours for about $10
items.author: Daniel van Strien
items.summary: Daniel van Strien asked Claude Opus to find a small OCR model and fix its doom loops with a budget of 5 hours and $100 on Hugging Face Jobs. The edit changed 0.0085% of weights with no training, and the model now reads a 1881 page instead of writing 16,399 characters of dots.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: tell an agent the failure you see, set a time and dollar budget, and let it repair the model directly.

items.title: Harness Leaderboard: nine coding-agent harnesses compared on open models across 28,849 trials
items.author: Joel Niklaus
items.summary: Joel Niklaus fixed model, provider and reasoning effort and changed only the harness, with three attempts per task.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: before picking a model, run your own tasks through several harnesses with the model held fixed.

items.title: Raschka's Open October roundup covers 10 open LLM architecture releases from one month
items.author: Sebastian Raschka
items.summary: Sebastian Raschka walks through each, starting with Kolibri-1 (78B), which uses grouped-query and sliding-window attention, and Ling 3.1 Flash (560B).
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: skim an expert's monthly roundup, then pick the one open model that fits your hardware and try it.

items.title: Ethan Mollick argues concern about AI verification is overstated and shares data from recent models
items.author: Ethan Mollick
items.summary: He posted charts from recent model results to make the case that people overweight the worry.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: run a 20-question check of your own domain facts on the model you use, then decide how much to trust it.

sections.title: AI for Science

items.title: Mistral Large 4 wrote a quantum chemistry SCF solver from scratch and built a 3D orbital view around it
items.author: Mistral AI
items.summary: From a short prompt, the model wrote a self-consistent field solver, validated its output, chose how to break the molecule and which orbitals to show, and built the 3D view.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: ask a model to write the solver, validate it against a known answer, and wrap it in an interactive view.

items.title: Anthropic: AI could take on 27 to 52% of researcher time per study, median 38%, with field speedups from 1.41x to 2.02x
items.author: Ethan Mollick
items.summary: Based on 207,049 sessions from Aug 2 to Sep 30, 2026. Estimated acceleration is 1.41x in chemistry, 1.96x in computer science and 2.02x in statistics, and physical steps make up 38 to 41% of time in chemistry and materials science.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: split your own workflow into steps, mark which are digital and which are physical, and automate the digital ones first.

items.title: BioBasicsBench tests agents on 100 real wet-lab analysis tasks, built with Ligo
items.author: OpenAI
items.summary: Tasks come from real experiments and ask whether agents can interpret raw lab data, identify errors and recognize when evidence does not support a conclusion.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: build a 100-task benchmark from your own real work and use it to pick tools.

items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: give an agent your data and ask it to propose three candidate models and fit each.

items.title: Mistral Large 4 joins Open Math OS, a research workspace for mathematicians and agents on open models

items.author: Kling AI

items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: storyboard a genre that is hard to shoot and generate it.

items.title: Claude Code edited a video end to end, from picking quotes and clips to cuts, zooms, music, text and upscaling
items.author: Ahmad
items.summary: Ahmad Osman says Opus 5.5 produced the whole thing.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: give an agent raw footage and a quote list and ask for a finished edit.

items.title: Asahi Linux bans generative AI contributions; DHH and Peter Steinberger say that is the wrong call
items.author: DHH
items.summary: Asahi's policy broadly forbids using generative AI for material contributions, citing harms to software freedom, the open-source community, the environment, privacy, user consent and developers, plus clean-room reverse-engineering concerns. DHH says Omarchy's Apple Silicon work, which uses agents and expanded on Asahi's, now faces rejected upstreaming. Steipete argues the project began by opening up closed systems and that a new restriction cuts against that.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: write down your team's rule for AI-assisted contributions in one page so contributors know where they stand.

items.title: Sutton says brute force is not enough and new methods are needed; roon says any spark of ability means superhuman within months to years
items.author: Richard Sutton
items.summary: Richard Sutton: 'Brute force computation is not enough for intelligence. Clever new methods are needed. The science of AI is far from finished.' Elvis Saravia agrees and expects a new algorithmic paradigm. roon, days earlier: any spark of an ability means months to years from superhuman, 'today grade school math, tomorrow Navier-Stokes', and it is hard to overhype.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: split your own roadmap into bets that ride scale and bets that need a new method, and fund both.

suggested_refinements.notes: Access: X search and a logged-in timeline were not available. Posts came from api.fxtwitter.com profile timelines for about 174 handles (about 20 recent posts each, not full chronological feeds), so the viral sweep covers handles queried only. Window: Nov 2 00:00 ET to Nov 8 23:59 ET. These handles returned 404: DarioAmodei, arthurmensch, xai, aider_ai, LangChainAI, ChatGPTapp, lovable_dev, elevenlabsio, heygen_official, CanvaAI, NotebookLM, MicrosoftCopilot, huggingface_hub, ccanonne_, chatgpt21, benedictevans, ProfessorPlum. Materials-science and building-science posts were thin on X this week; nearest items are OpenAI's physical engineering post, Maket Text to Furniture, the FreeCAD MCP demo, Anthropic's researcher-time data and Mistral's chemistry solver. Security and policy posts (OpenAI's Linux kernel pipeline, GPT-6 Cyber, DeepMind's RSA research) were left for the Research tab. Engagement counts were captured Nov 9 and keep rising. Top Pick pages verified: Claude Personal Finance, Get Maine Lobster, PSI proof, Anthropic vault, OpenAI Images 2.6, OpenAI physical engineering, authors' weight-space blog and the Hugging Face checkpoint.
